description: ERP shift calendar (GET /api/calendar -> week_pattern): per department x ISO weekday x shift the working-time window and its breaks. Supersedes the pre-next2.0 descriptor of the same sourceId, which was never in the active source set — it targeted the retired SMProfile-ShiftWindow under profiles/business/ and declared a `syntheticId` key that NO service implements (grepped across all of i3x-v4 services/ on 2026-08-03: zero hits), so it would have been accepted by source-schema.json (additionalProperties: true) and silently ignored at runtime. This descriptor uses `primaryKeyColumns`, which the it-edge really honours via change-detect.pkOf/encodeCompositePk. THE CALENDAR IS THE ANSWER TO 'WAS ANYTHING SUPPOSED TO RUN?': without it a consumer cannot separate an unscheduled hour from a failed one, and a weekend reads as an outage — see the profile description for the measurement that forced this source into the active set. full_refresh: the endpoint serves the complete 45-row week pattern on every call and honours no `since` param (verified 2026-08-03); the it-edge dedups via the per-key HWM, so a pattern that does not change emits nothing. Polled hourly — this is master data that changes when the plant changes its shift model, not per shift. 2026-08-18 (CAPT-RETRACT): polling.paginate ENABLED. it-edge (DATA-7) refused every delete/tombstone pass on this source with reason unpaginated_full_refresh — once an HOUR, matching intervalMs exactly (measured at 14:12:19Z, 15:12:19Z, 16:12:19Z, always seenCount 45 / trackedCount 45 / wouldHaveRetracted 0) — so the source could ingest but never RETRACT, and a shift pattern retired upstream (is_active = FALSE) would have stayed in the KG for ever. THE SUBTLETY THAT MADE THIS ONE DIFFERENT: this endpoint already served the COMPLETE population on every call — the statement had no LIMIT clause at all — so, unlike the articles/customers pair, nothing was being truncated. But serving everything is not PROVING you served everything, and that gap is the whole of DATA-7: a server-side default cap is invisible in the response, so the poller cannot tell 'all 45 rows there are' from 'the first 45 of more'. The endpoint ignored paging outright: MEASURED against the live ERP .154:38260, ?limit=5 -> 45 and ?offset=999 -> 45, with /api/orders?limit=5 -> 5 as the positive control in the same run. Fixed upstream first: sim-v5 api-erp d079f0ce (F-CALENDAR-PAGINATION), deployed to PROD as image tag 103145bd. VERIFIED on PROD after that deploy, with the same positive control in the same run: baseline -> 45, ?limit=5 -> 5, ?offset=45 -> 0, ?offset=999 -> 0. Paged exactly the way it-edge pages (advance by the rows actually returned, stop on an EMPTY page) at this descriptor's batchSize of 200: page 1 -> 45 rows, page 2 -> 0 rows, TOTAL 45 rows / 45 distinct / 0 duplicates. So the completeness proof costs exactly TWO requests an hour over a 5,559-byte payload — measured, not estimated. The ORDER BY upstream is (department_id, day_of_week, shift_id), which is this source's declared primaryKeyColumns and is a total order over the population: 45 rows / 45 distinct, measured in erp.shift_weekly_pattern WHERE is_active = TRUE. Immutable master data in a total order means the page windows can neither overlap nor skip. ONE COMPANION CHANGE WAS REQUIRED UPSTREAM AND IT MATTERS MORE THAN THE PAGING: the handler used to answer 200 {week_pattern: []} when its query threw (catch { pattern = []; }). Harmless while nobody could act on it — but an EMPTY FIRST PAGE is a positive statement to it-edge (population exhausted, fetch COMPLETE, retract every tracked key the fetch did not return), so enabling paginate would have turned one transient database hiccup into a tombstone for all 45 shift windows and erased the plant's working calendar. It now answers 503 calendar_unavailable and it-edge aborts the poll on the non-2xx, costing one skipped hourly poll instead of a silent deletion. intervalMs stays at 3600000 and batchSize at 200: this change is scoped to the retraction proof and alters no cadence.
